requirement: The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every place that inserts badge HTML escapes names and link targets and percent-encodes the Shields.io URL components.

**Obligation 1: escape requirement names when inserting badge HTML.**
- `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs:280) computes `escaped_name = escape_html(&full_name)`. It uses that value in the badge element's `id`.
- `shield_badge` (src/lib.rs:537) escapes the label and message in the `alt` text with `escape_html`.
- `reference_badge` (src/lib.rs:452) escapes the built-in's `title` text.
- `replace_query_directives` (src/lib.rs:376) and `render_detail_sections` (src/index.rs:677) also build badges through `shield_badge`, so they get the same escaping.
- `escape_html` (src/lib.rs:884) handles `& < > " '`.

**Obligation 2: escape link targets when inserting badge HTML.**
- `reference_badge` wraps `chapter_href(...)` in `escape_html`.
- `replace_definitions` escapes `detail_href` the same way. That value is used in both the badge anchor and the "See evidence" link.

**Obligation 3: encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components.**
- `shield_badge` passes both through `shield_path_component` (src/lib.rs:552).
- That function keeps only alphanumerics and `.`. It maps space to `_`, `_` to `__` and `-` to `--`, and percent-encodes every other byte. Punctuation therefore cannot change the URL structure.
- The final URL is also HTML-escaped when placed in `src`.

**Tests:**
- `badge_urls_percent_encode_punctuation_and_html_is_escaped` (src/lib.rs:1243) asserts the encoded URL for `/ ? # % & < > " '` and non-ASCII input. It also asserts the escaped `alt` text.
- `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` (src/lib.rs:1371) asserts `_` and `-` doubling and space-to-underscore. It carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.
- `reference_link_targets_are_escaped` (src/lib.rs:1262) asserts the `href` escaping through `reference_badge` with a path containing `& " < >`.

**Caveat:** no test covers the `replace_definitions` name or detail-href escaping with special characters. Valid names cannot contain HTML-special characters, and the source comment says that escaping is only a guard. Those call sites pass straight into the `escape_html` function that the tests above exercise, so I did not treat this as a gap.
